thread:
sara: Heads-up — bringing Zephyra LoRA merge into int4 shadow for customer evals. Quick eval pack (cust-invoice-50) flagged a consistent drop in amount extraction.
devin: Can you paste the quick numbers?
sara: Quick diff (baseline vs merged-int4):\n- baseline (zephyra-base-v2 + cust-lora unquantized): F1=0.92, amount-exact=98.7%\n- merged + q4_0 int4: F1=0.86, amount-exact=92.1%\nOnly ~50 examples but reproducible across 3 seeds.
oliver: Any tokenizer drift/offsets? That usually bites numeric stuff.
sara: Found a few examples where currency tokens get split oddly. Tokenize snippet:\n```\n>>> tokenizer.tokenize('€1,200.00')\n['Ġ', '€', '1', ',', '200', '.', '00']\n```\nResulting model output spaces numbers: "1 , 200 ." instead of "1,200.00". Looks like pretokenization/normalization not preserved after LoRA merge.
devin: Which quant backend / compile profile are you using? q4_0 vs q8_0 changes token alignment sometimes.
sara: q4_0 via our compile profile. Model ids: zephyra-base-v2 + lora:cust/zephyra-invoice-v1 hash=abc123. Merge done with postfusion merge script (v2.1.4) — default options.
eva: Are there failing examples in the pack we can use as regression tests?
sara: Yep, added 3 failing cases to the pack and pushed to the eval bucket. I also attached example where a decimal loses trailing zeros.
qa-bot: Created ticket ML-7891 with attached failing examples and perf logs. Severity: medium; assigned to eng-ml triage.
ci-bot: Shadow deployed to gpu-pool-2 (dedicated) for A/B. No OOM, latency +4ms p95, throughput unchanged. Shadow run id: shd-17182.
oliver: Quick hypothesis: LoRA merge script dropped a tokenizer normalization mapping (NFD/NFC or pretokenize compose). Try rerun with tokenizer-normalize flag or regenerate merged tokenizer with preserve_pretokenize=True.
sara: Running a quick rerun now: `redwood eval run --model zephyra-lora-abc123 --quant q4_0 --prompt-set cust-invoice-50 --tokenizer-normalize compose`
sara: Rerun results: int4 + normalize => F1=0.90, amount-exact=96.0% (much better). int8 fallback recovers to F1=0.91. So normalization is the main culprit; int4 quantization amplifies the token-split brittleness.
devin: OK — fix plan: regenerate merged tokenizer with normalization map preserved, roll new merge artifact, and run full quickpack. If results match baseline (<=1% delta) we can unblock canary.
oliver: I'll add a small helper to the merge script to set `preserve_pretokenize=True` and reapply `normalize_map` from base model. Pushing branch now.
sara: Will run the new quickpack when you push. ETA ~30m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
eva: Add a note to release docs and block canary until merge is validated. :no_entry_sign:
